recruitment: Reported inconsistently within the document: abstract states 11/01/2013–16/09/2015, while Methods states 01/11/2013 and 16/09/2015; flagged as a discrepancy in the source document
age: Not reported (only age range specified as ≤1 year old; no mean/median value given)
age_groups: Neonates and Infants (≤1 year old, per inclusion criteria)
sample_size: 22 cardiac arrest and 206 control patients ≤1 year old in the original cohort; after excluding 6 cardiac arrest patients with insufficient pre-arrest data, the model was trained and evaluated on 16 cardiac arrest cases and 48 age/gender-matched controls (1:3 ratio) — 11 cardiac arrest + 33 controls in training, 5 cardiac arrest + 15 controls in test

outcome_raw: Cardiac arrest defined per The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database as "the cessation of effective cardiac mechanical function"; cases identified via ICD discharge codes and validated by expert clinician (manual adjudication) review of electronic health records

prediction_horizon: At least 2h warning; mean 17h (SD 7.5) among 16 cases; not a fixed 17h forecast
threshold: ROC-derived per bootstrap iteration; examples 0.5/0.56 are not a common fixed threshold

title:
Predicting Cardiac Arrest in Children with Heart Disease: A
Novel Machine Learning Algorithm Model 1 - Functional Gradient Boosting (RDN Boost) Model
study_aim: To evaluate whether a machine learning algorithm (functional gradient boosting, RDN Boost) can accurately predict in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) in children admitted to a single-center pediatric CICU, using routinely collected EHR data, and to compare this against a traditional multivariable logistic regression model.
design: Single-center retrospective cohort study
setting: Single-center pediatric cardiac intensive care unit (CICU), University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, TX
age_groups: Children (all patients <18 years of age); no further breakdown into neonate/infant/children subgroups reported
sample_size: 160 index cardiac arrest events; 711 unique control patients (approximately 41,000 hours of data total)
ca_prevalence: Case-control ratio approximately 1:5 (160 cases:711 controls) after exclusions; background CICU IHCA rate stated as 3 events per 1000 patient days (~20 IHCA events/year)
conditions: Congenital and acquired heart disease; patients with single-ventricle physiology and non-single-ventricle physiology; both surgical and medical CICU admissions included; IHCA patients more likely to have single-ventricle physiology and higher STAT category surgical procedures
architecture_raw: Gradient boosting (functional gradient boosting via RDN Boost — a relational/non-parametric ensemble algorithm; relational extension of XGBoost)
modality_raw: Multimodal — vital signs and laboratory values (11 variables); vital signs (e.g. BP, HR, O2 sats), demographics, ventilator settings, urine output, echocardigram parameters and medications also collected but final model used 11 vital sign/lab variables
feature_selection: XGBoost used to identify the most important features from the full candidate set; top 11 features selected based on split criteria
predictors: 11 (heart rate, vasoactive-inotrope score [VIS], SpO₂, urine output, diastolic blood pressure, ETCO₂, cerebral oximetry [rSO₂c], somatic oximetry [rSO₂s], anion gap, base excess, FiO₂)
time_series: Yes — data collected in 4-hour increments up to 16 hours prior to IHCA (cases) or last 16 hours of admission (controls); model designed to update ("anytime" capability) as more data accumulate
internal_validation: 5-fold cross-validation
split_sizes: 80% training / 20% testing per fold (5-fold cross-validation); no separate external test set
frequency_raw: Continuous/"anytime" — model can be queried at any time point once at least 4 hours of data are available, with predictions improving as more data accumulate
auroc_raw: 0.85 [95% CI 0.79, 0.90] at 1 hour prior to CA (peak performance); values also reported at 13, 9, and 5 hours prior (see Table 1 subgroup analyses; overall model AUROC lower at more distal time points, improving as time to arrest decreased)
lead_time_raw: Model queried at multiple time points up to 13 hours prior to arrest; peak performance reported at 1 hour prior to CA
outcome_raw: Actual arrest — in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) resulting in CPR, captured from a local CPR event database; index events only
comparator_raw: Compared against (a) logistic regression model (AUC 0.83 at 1 hour prior to CA) and (b) Gaussian Naïve Bayes classifier (AUROC lower than gradient boosting model across all time points, per Figure 3); PPV 36%, NPV 97% (for gradient boosting model, from confusion matrix); no comparison to PEWS or other monitoring systems reported
validation_type: 5-fold cross-validation
prediction_horizon: 1h extracted peak AUROC; other 5/9/13h results not numerically supplied

study_aim: To use machine learning to predict in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) in pediatric ICU patients up to three hours in advance, using a combination of ECG-derived heart rate variability metrics, vital signs time series, medications, and demographics.
design: Single-center retrospective pilot study
setting: Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), Johns Hopkins Hospital, Baltimore, Maryland
age_groups:

5 Years–11 Years (n=267, 1 IHCA), 
11 Years–18 Years (n=388, 4 IHCA); cohort also included 38 patients aged 18+ (0 IHCA)
sample_size: 1,145 patients total (15 experienced IHCA); resulted in 14,714 five-minute time windows (516 labeled positive for IHCA) used for model training/validation/testing. ca_prevalence: 15/1,145 patients (1.3%) at patient level; 516/14,714 windows (3.5%) at window level
modality_raw: Multimodal — ECG waveform-derived HRV metrics, vital signs summary statistics, medication (therapeutic drug class) data, and demographics
feature_selection: Features missing from more than 10% of sample windows were removed; non-binary features normalized using two-step z-score normalization (first by age group relative to negative-sample mean/SD, then standard z-score)

internal_validation: Data split into training, validation, and testing sets at the patient level (732/184/229 patients); optimal classification threshold selected from validation-set ROC curve
split_sizes: Training: 732 patients (6 IHCA); Validation: 184 patients (4 IHCA); Testing (held-out): 229 patients (5 IHCA)
frequency_raw: Continuous — non-overlapping 5-minute window predictions
lead_time_raw: Up to 3 hours prior to IHCA onset (3-hour window chosen as it outperformed a 1-hour prediction window)

validation_type: Data split into training, validation, and testing sets at the patient level (732/184/229 patients); optimal classification threshold selected from validation-set ROC curve
prediction_horizon: 5min windows labelled positive within 3h before CA; 3h preferred over 1h
threshold: Validation ROC optimal operating point; numeric threshold not_reported

study_aim: To determine if a model utilizing regional cerebral oximetry (rSO2c) and somatic oximetry (rSO2s), alongside other clinical variables, could predict cardiac arrest (CA) in children admitted to a single-center pediatric cardiac intensive care unit (CICU).
design: Single-center retrospective case-control study
setting: Pediatric cardiac intensive care unit (CICU), Children's Medical Center Dallas — a 26-bed unit admitting surgical and non-surgical patients with heart disease
age:
Cardiac arrest group: median 54 days [IQR 1–908 days
 No cardiac arrest (control) group: median 217 days [IQR 30–1,563]; P < 0.0001
age_groups: Mixed — reported as median age in days with wide IQR spanning neonates through older children
sex:
Cardiac arrest group: 76/160 (47.5%) female (calculated from 84/160 = 52.50% male)
Control group: 344/711 (48.38%) female (calculated from 367/711 = 51.62% male); P = 0.84 (not significant)
sample_size: 160 cardiac arrest (case) patients; 711 control patients; total N = 871
ca_prevalence: 160/871 (18.4%) in this case-control cohort (not a natural population prevalence, as cases and controls were selected via case-control design)
conditions: Congenital heart disease (surgical and non-surgical patients); single ventricle physiology significantly more common in CA group (64/160, 40.0%) vs. controls (91/711, 12.80%), P < 0.0001; for surgical patients, CA group had higher STAT mortality categories, longer CPB times (median 118.0 vs. 77.0 minutes, P < 0.0001), and longer cross-clamp times (median 70.0 vs. 49.5 minutes, P = 0.003)
architecture_raw: Logistic regression (baseline comparator) — described as a multivariable logistic regression model
modality_raw: Multimodal — vital signs, laboratory values, and NIRS (near-infrared spectroscopy) oximetry data (rSO2c, rSO2s), plus vasoactive medication data (VIS)
feature_selection: The 11 candidate variables were originally selected via a previously created XGBoost machine-learning algorithm (from a separate, unpublished study by the same group); of these, univariable analysis was performed on each variable, and only those significantly associated with CA were carried forward into the multivariable logistic regression model
predictors: 11 candidate variables considered (HR, SpO2, DBP, rSO2c, rSO2s, ETCO2, urine output, base excess, anion gap, FiO2, VIS); final multivariable model included 5 variables (SpO2-rSO2c difference, SpO2-rSO2s difference, HR, DBP, VIS); of these, 4 were independently significantly associated with CA (SpO2-rSO2s difference, HR, VIS, DBP) — SpO2-rSO2c difference was not significant
time_series: Yes — hourly averaged data analyzed across hours 1 through 15 prior to CA (for cases) or within the first 48 hours of admission (for controls); model performance (AUROC) calculated as a function of time before arrest
internal_validation: NR
frequency_raw: Hourly snapshot — hourly averaged values used, model evaluated at discrete hourly time points from 15 hours to 1 hour before CA (not continuous/high-frequency)
auroc_raw: 0.83 at 1 hour before CA (best/peak performance); AUROC increased over time as it approached the arrest, ranging from approximately 0.72–0.74 at 15–10 hours prior, rising to 0.83 at 1 hour prior (see Figure 1 for full hourly trend)
lead_time_raw: Evaluated at each hour from 1 to 15 hours prior to CA; peak/best performance reported at 1 hour prior to CA
outcome_raw: Actual arrest — cardiac arrest defined per the Get With The Guidelines Resuscitation (GWTGR) Registry as pulselessness or pulse with inadequate perfusion requiring chest compressions and/or defibrillation; study included only arrests resulting in chest compressions (excluded defibrillation-only events without compressions); index events only, confirmed via EHR chart review
validation_type: NR
prediction_horizon: 1h extracted peak; 1-15h evaluated, distal ranges approximate only
threshold: SpO2-rSO2s cutoff 29% applies to a predictor, not established as multivariable model threshold
